text:
marie: heads up, running into a weird parity bug between mobile SDK and server redaction pipeline. mobile crash reports show PII (emails) in logs even though server-side redaction is enabled :cry:
aj: can you repro locally? steps?
marie: yep, minimal repro in kotlin sampleapp. pattern: when coroutines + okhttp retries are used, the request-id we attach in an interceptor sometimes doesn't make it to the backend. server redaction is keyed off request-id -> pii lookup, so missing id = no redaction.
aj: ah interesting. so header gets dropped on retry or across suspend boundaries?
marie: seems both. example: we set X-Request-Id in an okhttp interceptor using MDC/context, but when suspend functions resume on a different thread the MDC is lost before retry triggers. also okhttp's retry interceptor rebuilds the call and our header-setting logic isn't always executed.
samir: do you have a small snippet? might be the common coroutine -> thread-local problem.
marie: snippet from sampleapp:```kotlin
// in Interceptor
override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
  val id = MDC.get("requestId") ?: UUID.randomUUID().toString()
  val newReq = chain.request().newBuilder()
    .addHeader("X-Request-Id", id)
    .build()
  return chain.proceed(newReq)
}
// elsewhere we set MDC in coroutine context before suspend call
MDC.put("requestId", reqId)
myApiClient.post(...)
```
marie: repro steps attached in sampleapp: run with flaky network, trigger retry path, check server logs for request id missing.
lina: two orthogonal fixes: 1) explicitly propagate request id as a request header from the call site instead of relying on MDC/threadlocals; 2) adopt OpenTelemetry context propagation so the value follows suspend/resume and thread hops.
aj: agree. quick patch: ensure call-site sets header on the request builder so retries copy it. e.g., `request.newBuilder().header("X-Request-Id", reqId).build()` on the client call. less fragile.
samir: we also have an internal otel-context bridge for okhttp that does Context.current() -> header propagation. could plumb that into the mobile SDK. Lina, is that library kotlin-friendly?
lina: yes, there's an otel-context-propagation artifact that works with coroutines + okhttp. needs small adapter to propagate into MDC if you want legacy logs to see it.
marie: another wrinkle: when request id is missing, our redaction queue reports failures because the downstream enricher expects id to lookup pii mapping. ops-bot alerted earlier: `alert: redaction-failure-queue > 200` — saw that spike around 03:12.
ops-bot: incident: redaction-failure-queue size 237 -> paging on-call.
aj: can we short-term mitigate by setting mobile SDK client default logging level to INFO in release builds (we currently ship DEBUG for some internal betas), so fewer PII-y debug logs are generated?
marie: we already flipped debug->info in canary yesterday for beta channel, saw a ~60% drop in raw PII logs. but still need to fix propagation for correctness.
samir: action items: 1) marie to open a sampleapp PR with explicit header propagation + test that retries preserve header (small reproducer), 2) lina to evaluate otel-context-propagation integration for mobile SDK, 3) aj to add server-side defensive check: if no X-Request-Id, attempt to use alternative trace id for redaction lookup as fallback, and emit metric.
marie: will open PR w/ test and attach trace logs. planning to run canary with header fix then roll out widely.
lina: FYI also found an edge case where okhttp's connection pool replay on 401 sometimes replays without custom headers; will add comment in PR.
aj: thanks — assigning follow-ups in Jira.
marie: TL;DR: bug caused by coroutine/threadlocal context loss + okhttp retry behavior. short fix: attach header at call site; long fix: use proper OTEL context propagation. keeping ticket updated. :lock: :white_check_mark:
